properties.name: One sentence of a node's text can change, or a dated note be appended, without re-sending the field — and never without the revision guard
properties.statement: Anthony, 2026-09-18, promoting flo2's F3/F4 (the third project to report it after qs and dev_storyflow, 2026-09-04): settling a decision whose options live in prose — which the brainstorm skill asks for on purpose — meant re-sending a 6 KB body to move one line, or leaving 'Options, none chosen' standing false. Measured on reflow2's own design: 210 of 743 decisions exceed 4 KB, 164 carry dated ═══ sections, 92 preserved re-sends. The edit must be bounded: the text to replace occurs exactly once or the call is refused with the count and nothing is written; omitting it appends after a blank line; the prior state is preserved and the reply names what moved, exactly as every other write. Graph text stays data: the caller supplies both strings, and the server never reads a node's prose for meaning.
